newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: CYCLONE THREAT MOVING WEST
With tropical cyclone Rachel moving further into the Timor Sea this afternoon, the Weather Bureau says strong winds and heavy rain around Darwin today should begin to ease.
The cylcone is now 230 kilometres west of Darwin.
It is expected to intensify into a category two cyclone within 12 hours, bringing destructive winds gusting up to 150 kilometres an hour to the north Kimberley coast, in Western Australia.
Duty forecaster, Geoff Doull, says Darwin and the western Top End have probably seen the worst of the bad weather.
A cyclone warning is still current between Croker Island in the Northern Territory and Kuri Bay in Western Australia.
FOUR CHARGED AFTER ADELAIDE DRUG DEATH
Adelaide police have arrested four people - and reported a fifth - following the drug-related death of a woman at Mitchell Park on New Year's Day.
A 21-year-old Aberfoyle Park man has been charged with supplying a drug of dependence, and cultivating cannabis.
A 27-year-old woman and a 31-year-old man face charges of possessing cannabis and amphetamines for sale.
Another man, aged 24; and a women, aged 21; were charged with minor drug offences.
KENNETT: MINIMALIST REPUBLIC A BAD IDEA
Victorian Premier, Jeff Kennett, says Acting Prime Minister Tim Fischer's proposal for a republic is fraught with danger.
Mr Fischer has suggested a "minimalist model", giving the Chief Justice of the High Court, power to appoint and dismiss the Governor General, on the Prime Minister's advice.
Mr Kennett says the proposal would seriously undermine the distance between the Government and judiciary.
The Premier says Mr Fischer's minimalist approach will have a minimal life-span.
INSURANCE COUNCIL WARNS HOLIDAY MAKERS TO LOCK-UP
The Insurance Council of Australia is warning holiday-makers to ensure their homes are locked up before they go away.
Figures from insurers show many householders are forgetting to activate house alarms, while 15-percent of people going on holiday still leave their homes unlocked.
The Council's Mark Sheehan says people should make sure they don't leave spare keys outside, cancel deliveries, and install light timers.
He says householders should also make sure their home insurance is up to date.
